summary_paragraph: A male patient, 21 days post orthotopic liver transplant for cryptogenic cirrhosis, was readmitted with fever, hypotension, and worsening back and abdominal pain. Imaging revealed left upper lobe ground-glass opacities consistent with early pneumonia and a large subphrenic fluid collection. He was started on Vancomycin and Cefepime based on prior Enterococcus bacteremia. A cervical spine MRI ruled out spinal infection, showing only degenerative changes. A PICC line was placed to complete intravenous antibiotic therapy at an extended care facility. His condition improved with treatment, inflammatory markers decreased, and he regained mobility with minimal assistance. He was discharged back to rehabilitation with plans for continued IV antibiotics, tube feeds, and close monitoring of transplant and metabolic parameters.
